name: Pell Sethry
role: Cord-and-hemp seller of the east market — Sela's mother, and a slow public decider
appearance: Middle-aged, hemp-dust in the weave of everything she owns, forearms corded from forty years of hauling line. Stands at her own stall rather than behind it.
physicality: Her body decides before she does — a heel up, weight forward, the posture of somebody about to resolve. When the heel goes down the arithmetic is finished and the direction is not yet named.
voiceHints: Weighs a thing out loud in counts and then stops talking. Will not be hurried to the end of it.
wants: To be sure before she is public, because in the east market being public is the whole of it.
fears: Naming someone and being wrong in front of the people who buy from her.
knowledge: Every cord and line supplier in the east market and what each of them is quietly short of
That Fendt is named — a specific person responsible, not an anonymous system
That Orla made a deliberate choice at personal cost, and that the evidence did not arrive casually

reactsToReputation.any: prices you fairly and says little
reactsToReputation.honest: tells you what she is weighing and lets you watch
reactsToReputation.pushy: the heel goes down and the conversation is over

questSeeds: She is deciding something in public and the market is counting with her
Sela is her daughter and is not in the market
